claims.text: Synergistic block of sequential steps in bacterial folate metabolism:
claims.quote: The antibiotics act synergistically to block sequential steps in bacterial folate metabolism:

claims.text: TMP stops dihydrofolate → tetrahydrofolate; SMX inhibits PABA → dihydropteroate.
claims.quote: Trimethoprim (TMP) prevents reduction of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate. - Sulfamethoxazole (SMX) inhibits conversion of p-aminobenzoic acid to dihydropteroate.

claims.text: Nausea, vomiting, rash most often; more ADRs in AIDS (fever, rash, neutropenia).
claims.quote: Nausea, vomiting, and rash occur most often. Patients with AIDS have a high incidence of adverse effects, especially fever, rash, and neutropenia.
claims.locator: Adverse Effects of TMP and SMX

claims.text: Serious: SJS/TEN, DRESS, hepatic necrosis, agranulocytosis/aplastic anemia: stop at the first rash.
claims.quote: BACTRIM should be discontinued at the first appearance of skin rash or any sign of a serious adverse reaction. A skin rash may be followed by a more severe reaction, such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, DRESS, AFND, AGEP, hepatic necrosis, or serious blood disorders

claims.text: Hyperkalemia (high-dose TMP for PCP, renal insufficiency, K-raising drugs).
claims.quote: P. jirovecii pneumonia, induces a progressive but reversible increase of serum potassium concentrations in a substantial number of patients. Even treatment with recommended doses may cause hyperkalemia when trimethoprim is administered to patients with underlying disorders of potassium metabolism, with renal insufficiency, or if drugs known to induce hyperkalemia are given concomitantly.
Folate deficiency (resulting in macrocytic anemia) can also occur.
claims.locator: Adverse Effects of TMP and SMX

claims.quote: TMP competitively inhibits renal tubular creatinine secretion and may cause an artificial increase in serum creatinine, although glomerular filtration rate remains unchanged.
claims.locator: Adverse Effects of TMP and SMX

claims.quote: In glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficient individuals, hemolysis may occur. This reaction is frequently dose-related.

claims.text: Hypersensitivity to TMP or sulfonamides; prior drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia; megaloblastic anemia from folate deficiency; age <2 months; marked hepatic damage; severe renal insufficiency without monitoring; dofetilide.
claims.quote: BACTRIM is contraindicated in the following situations: a known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides history of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia with use of trimethoprim and/or sulfonamides documented megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency pediatric patients less than 2 months of age marked hepatic damage severe renal insufficiency when renal function status cannot be monitored concomitant administration with dofetilide

claims.text: Pregnancy: avoid in first trimester (neural tube defects) and near term (kernicterus).
claims.quote: use of TMP/SMX should be avoided during the first trimester (because neural tube defects are a risk) and near term. If used during pregnancy or in neonates, TMP/SMX increases blood levels of unconjugated bilirubin and increases risk of kernicterus in the fetus or neonate.
claims.locator: Use of TMP and SMX During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Raises warfarin effect and phenytoin, methotrexate and rifampin levels.
claims.quote: TMP/SMX may increase warfarin activity and levels of phenytoin, methotrexate, and rifampin.
claims.locator: Dosing Considerations for TMP and SMX

claims.text: Hyperkalemia with ACE inhibitors (case reports in elderly).
claims.quote: In the literature, three cases of hyperkalemia in elderly patients have been reported after concomitant intake of BACTRIM and an angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor.

claims.text: PCP: avoid leucovorin (treatment failure, excess mortality).
claims.quote: Treatment failure and excess mortality were observed when BACTRIM was used concomitantly with leucovorin for the treatment of HIV positive patients with P. jirovecii pneumonia in a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
claims.locator: Warnings › Risk Associated with Concurrent Use of Leucovorin
